query: I'm running bash on WSL and my GH_TOKEN env var seems to be empty — how do I confirm it's set without printing the whole token to the terminal?
We're onboarding a new hire to the project and I need to verify their AWS credentials on their laptop. What commands should I walk them through in terminal without exposing their secret access key?
Our CI is failing with 401 on the GitHub API but works locally. How do I compare the local and CI GH_TOKEN values to see if they're actually the same secret or if rotation got out of sync?

gcloud auth application-default login just finished but my Python service still gets 'unauthenticated' errors. I want to debug what access token the SDK is picking up — what's the safe way to do this from pwsh?

I copy-pasted my STRIPE_SECRET_KEY from 1Password into my .env file and the Stripe API keeps rejecting it. How can I check if there's a trailing newline or the length is off, without echoing the key itself?

Write me a PowerShell one-liner a junior dev can run to confirm OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and GH_TOKEN are all set in their shell environment. They paste the output into Slack so obviously don't print the values.

We just rotated OPENAI_API_KEY in prod. From my SSH session I want to prove that the prod container actually picked up the new key and not the old one that's still in my local env. Think comparing fingerprints.

curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges is dumping my Stripe key into the trace output on every run. How do I debug this request differently without leaking the bearer header?
I have two different .envrc files across two machines and I want to diff which keys are defined in each one without ever showing the values. bash please.
Azure az login feels stale — how do I verify the currently-active account and subscription without ending up with a raw access token in my shell history or PSReadLine history file?
Explain how transformer tokenization handles subword units. Specifically, how does BPE differ from WordPiece in terms of how token boundaries get determined during training?

In our MMORPG we have a 'soul token' drop mechanic — players earn tokens from raid bosses and spend them at an NPC merchant. Help me design the drop-rate formula so 95th-percentile playtime gets ~3 tokens per week.
Read the file adr/0071-direnv.md and summarize what decision was made about using GH_TOKEN in that ADR. I'm just reviewing the history, no action needed.
What's the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow? I'm preparing slides for a KubeCon talk — theoretical overview, flow diagrams, no implementation or credentials involved.
Our internal JWT library benchmark shows it's 2x slower than jose. Can you profile the token verification path and suggest optimizations? Source is in packages/jwt/src/verify.ts.
How does rate limiting work on the GitHub API in general? I'm writing a blog post for our engineering site about primary vs secondary limits. Just need conceptual explanation, no code.
Can you write a C# enum called EPaymentProvider listing Stripe, PayPal, Bancontact, TossPayments? This is just the type definition for our PaymentService model layer.
Review the unit tests in tests/parse_bearer.test.ts — they cover a parser that validates the RFC-6750 bearer token format string. The tests themselves use fixture strings, no real secrets.
Our Slack bot posts daily standup reminders but it's silent on Tuesdays. Check cron/standup.yml — I suspect the cron expression has a wrong weekday field. Nothing to do with the bot token.

I'm reading 'Designing Data-Intensive Applications' chapter 5 on replication. Can you explain token-based request routing as a consistency concept? Purely conceptual, I'm not implementing anything this week.
